condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

description.narrative: 1.A significant contribution made to the establishment of new forest PAs covering over 1.8 million hectares and to the strengthening of the management of new and existing forest PAs. 2.A number of innovative approaches, models, and techniques introduced, including the introduction of HCVF management practices, forest inventory and management planning that incorporates remote sensing data, the use of information technology for effective pasture management, public-private partnerships, economic valuation of ecological resources, and sustainable forest management incorporating climate change. 3. Multiple measures are undertaken to improve coordination amongst stakeholders with respect to biodiversity monitoring and wildlife law enforcement, and improve data management and knowledge dissemination.

comment.narrative: 1. There is not currently sufficient technical or financial capacity available to support the necessary process for expanding the protected area system of Kazakhstan to be appropriately representative of Kazakhstan’s forest ecosystems. 2.The current institutional framework of forest management units managed by regional governments is inefficient, and does not allow necessary strengthening of capacity for forest management. 3.There is currently poor coordination amongst national stakeholders responsible for biological monitoring, and wildlife law enforcement. In addition, data and information on biodiversity monitoring is not aggregated, or analyzed in a comprehensive way.

1. Creating a basis for a more representative of globally significant forest ecosystems of the Northern, Central and Western Tien Shan. 2. Improvement of the capacity and effectiveness of pilot protected areas. 3. Establish a framework for the sustainable management of high conservation value forests and improve the planning system of forest protection institutions. 4. Creation of a sustainable basis for saxaul forest cultivation. 5. Demonstration of landscape planning approaches and sustainable management of forest pastures in project areas. 6. Development of sustainable ecological tourism and introduction of additional ecological education. 7. Resource assessment of medicinal plants and assessment of the status of rare plant species in Altai. 8. Implementation of effective patrolling approaches using SMART at the pilot Pas. 9. Determination of the habitat, assessment of the status of the population of the snow leopard. 10. Improvement of the snow leopard monitoring system.

description.narrative: Degree to which policy and regulatory context for managing natural resources incorporates ecosystem services (at least one regulation adopted at provincial or national level that recognizes and incorporates TSA methodology)

comment.narrative: No methodology for considering full cost-benefit of ecosystem services incorporated in natural resource management policy and regulatory framework
Implemented 1 pilot project to assess the national forestry system using the TSA methodology

The project, throughout its entire implementation period, had one pilot project dedicated to assessing the national forestry system using the TSA (Total System of Assessment) methodology. The outcomes of this assessment were widely disseminated to numerous stakeholders, ranging from the FWC to the deputies of the Mazhilis of the Parliament.
At the national level, a methodological guide to the use of target scenario analysis tools for regional planning has been developed

To introduce the TSA approach into long-term development planning in Kazakhstan, guidelines on the use of target scenario analysis tools at the provincial/local level are being developed and integrated into natural resource management planning and sustainable sector development policies.
Also, to practically apply the TSA approach, efforts are underway to strengthen the national capacity to conduct economic and environmental assessments by developing a training module covering the 5-step approach of the methodology and testing it through training sessions.
To meet the indicator, the TSA methodology will be integrated into the biodiversity conservation concept currently being developed by the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan
